question: Which one of these could act as extrinsic motivation for a javelin thrower?
markScheme:
Correct answer: B - Gaining a medal for winning the javelin event.
1 mark for the correct option.
options: A - Feeling of pride at the distance of the throw recorded
B - Gaining a medal for winning the javelin event
C - Improved social status within the athletics club
D - Performing the javelin throw for enjoyment
correctOption: B - Gaining a medal for winning the javelin event

question: Motivation is used to increase the effort and persistence of a performer. Explain how a ski coach can use different forms of motivation to improve performance. Use examples to support your answer.
markScheme:
- Intrinsic motivation by setting goals/challenges that develop feelings of self-satisfaction/pride
- Extrinsic motivation by providing tangible rewards, eg medals/trophies/certificates
- Extrinsic motivation by providing intangible rewards, eg praise/applause/records
Max 3 marks.

question: Motivation is important for lacrosse players. Name and describe different forms of motivation.
markScheme:
A - Intrinsic - motivation from within/internal desire/want
B - Extrinsic - motivation from external sources/outside the player
C - (Extrinsic) tangible - physical rewards, eg trophies
D - (Extrinsic) intangible - non-physical rewards, eg praise
Max 3 marks.

question: Observational learning involves the stages of attention, retention, motor production and motivation. Using examples, name the two different types of extrinsic motivation.

question: Games players will practise to improve their skills, but to do this regularly requires motivation. (i) How does intrinsic motivation differ from extrinsic motivation?
markScheme:
Intrinsic from within/inside and extrinsic from outside. (If just 'intrinsic from within and extrinsic is not' this is too vague.) Intrinsic = drive/urge from within.
1 mark.

question: Games players will practise to improve their skills, but to do this regularly requires motivation. (ii) Explain why intrinsic motivation is thought to be a better form of motivation than extrinsic motivation.
markScheme:
- Intrinsic motivation gives the performer a sense of control over performance; concerned with self
- (Excessive) extrinsic motivation may reduce/lead to loss of intrinsic motivation/playing for the prize, not love of the game
- Performers demand increasing extrinsic rewards/some rewards become unimportant/lose their value
- Failure to achieve an extrinsic reward may lead to a loss of intrinsic motivation/if no reward, they give up
- Extrinsic motivation controls or manipulates behaviour/overly reliant
- (Excessive) need for extrinsic reward can lead to too much pressure/win at all costs/leads to cheating
('Extrinsic is no good' is too vague as it is in the question.)
Max 3 marks.

question: In order to learn a skill, a performer needs to be motivated. (i) What do you understand by the term 'intrinsic' motivation?
markScheme:
The will/want/desire/drive to win/achieve success/equivalent, that occurs within the performer/equivalent (accept examples - self-satisfaction/personal pride/etc). (Stating the reverse, such as 'it's not rewards', is too vague.)
Max 2 marks.

question: In order to learn a skill, a performer needs to be motivated. (ii) Explain the disadvantages of using 'extrinsic' motivation to motivate an individual.
markScheme:
(Excessive) extrinsic motivation may damage/lead to loss of intrinsic motivation/love of the activity/self-satisfaction (idea is too much extrinsic motivation is bad). Become dependent on/loss of extrinsic motivation (idea that extrinsic motivation controls you). Excessive extrinsic motivation eventually loses its effect/becomes worthless. Removal/failure to achieve extrinsic reward may lead to loss of motivation (not achieving enough for extrinsic motivation to work). Too much pressure, leading to cheating (accept 'win at all costs').
Max 2 marks.

question: In order to learn a skill, a performer needs to be motivated. (iii) How could a coach motivate a group of athletics squad members, of differing abilities, who regularly train together?
markScheme:
Allow success/handicap races/competitions/group similar abilities together (idea of competitions for success, NOT becoming competitive). Use of external rewards/prizes/equivalent. Make it fun/enjoyable. Use of role models. Use praise/verbal encouragement/reinforcement/positive feedback (not just feedback). Emphasise personal improvement/set personal goals/challenges. Avoid punishment. Immediate reinforcement for weaker performers. Attribute success internally.
Max 4 marks.

question: In order to improve their performance, badminton players need motivation. (i) Explain the meaning of the term 'motivation'.
markScheme:
The will/desire/drive/want to learn/achieve success/equivalent; Intrinsic - from within/self-satisfaction; Extrinsic - rewards; Tangible - touchable/eg; Non-tangible - not physical/equivalent.
Max 2 marks.

question: In order to improve their performance, badminton players need motivation. (ii) How could a coach motivate a badminton player to improve?
markScheme:
